text:
Winnipeg scored twice before the Canucks had settled in, and the night never got better for Vancouver.

Alex Iafallo tipped in a power-play goal at 3:49, and Cole Koepke scored at 4:03 on a wrist shot our numbers gave a 3% chance. Liam Ohgren pulled one back at 6:51, set up by Marco Rossi and Jonathan Lekkerimäki, on another 4% shot, but Dawson Mercer restored the two-goal cushion at 14:04 off a Cole Perfetti feed. Mercer finished with a goal and an assist and was the first star.

The second period is where Winnipeg's advantage became obvious. The Jets out-chanced Vancouver 1.59 expected goals to 0.57 (expected goals are the quality of the chances), and two of those turned into goals: Neal Pionk at 6:52 and Mark Scheifele, poking one in at 11:36. The secondary assist on Scheifele's goal went to Viggo Björck, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 draft out of Djurgårdens, for his first NHL point. Kyle Connor assisted on both second-period goals. Mario Ferraro added a sixth in the third, and Brock Boeser's late backhand was Vancouver's second.

The process behind it was clear. Winnipeg deserved to win 81% of replays (the share of replays of every shot a team wins), had 3.49 expected goals to Vancouver's 1.65, and forced the Canucks into 22 giveaways while taking the puck away eight times. Stuart Skinner had an easy night, 24 saves on 26 shots.

For Vancouver, it is four straight without a win (0-4-0), and Leevi Meriläinen's numbers will sting: six goals on 29 shots, 2.5 more than those shots deserved. That's the part that turned a loss into a rout. Rossi put seven shots on goal and kept trying. But a team that keeps losing the possession battle this badly will need more than its goalie to stop the slide, and the Jets showed what it looks like when a game tilts early and stays there.
headline: Jets rout the Canucks, and Vancouver's skid hits four
